content.value_statement: Argcfile syntax can be hard to edit because behavior is driven by structured Bash comments. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create accurate Argc command definitions.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required Argcfile comment tags for commands, arguments, options, flags, environment variables, and metadata.
Shows the standard argc initialization pattern used in Bash scripts.
Documents common forms for required, repeated, defaulted, and choice-based arguments.
Guides updates to Argcfile.sh files and scripts that use argc parsing.
Points users to upstream Argc specification, variable, and example documentation.
limitations: It does not install argc or verify that argc is present on the user system.
It does not execute or test generated shell scripts by itself.
It focuses on Argcfile syntax, not general Bash security review.
It assumes users trust the local argc binary used by their scripts.

use_cases.title: Add CLI Arguments
use_cases.description: Add positional arguments, flags, and options to an existing Argcfile with the correct comment tag format.

use_cases.title: Create Command Runners
use_cases.description: Build a small Bash command runner that exposes subcommands and generated help through argc.

use_cases.title: Document Argc Syntax
use_cases.description: Translate Argcfile examples into clear guidance for teams that maintain internal command scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Argcfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Argcfile.sh for a Bash command that accepts a required name argument and one verbose flag.

prompt_templates.title: Add Options to a Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this Argcfile to add a repeated --tag option, a --format choice option, and generated help text.

prompt_templates.title: Design Subcommands
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Argcfile command structure with build, test, and release subcommands. Include arguments, options, and metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Review Advanced Argc Syntax
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Argcfile for correct argc syntax, function-based defaults, choice helpers, environment variables, and metadata usage.

output_examples.input: A request to add a required file path, a repeated tag option, and a dry-run flag.
output_examples.output: The assistant describes the needed Argc tags, where they belong, and how each generated variable will be used.

output_examples.input: A request to create subcommands for build and deploy workflows.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines a Bash command layout with subcommand descriptions, scoped options, and metadata for required tools.

output_examples.input: A request to explain function-based choices in an Argcfile.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains that helper functions print candidates line by line and are referenced through argc comment syntax.

best_practices: Keep Argc comment tags close to the function or command they configure.
Use explicit required markers, defaults, and choices so generated help matches script behavior.
Review generated Bash before running it, especially when defaults or choices call helper functions.
anti_patterns: Do not mix unrelated shell comments into Argc tag blocks without clear descriptions.
Do not rely on argc variables without setting defaults or required markers for missing values.
Do not treat function-based defaults or choices as a substitute for reviewing Bash logic.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps create and modify Argcfile.sh files and Bash scripts that use argc comment tags.

faq.question: Does it install argc?
faq.answer: No. It only provides editing guidance and examples for files that use argc.

faq.question: Can it help with subcommands?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents the @cmd tag and related syntax for describing subcommands.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill text contains Bash examples, but it does not execute commands by itself.

faq.question: Can it explain environment variables?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers the @env tag and notes that argc validates existing environment variables.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
